bug_meta.title: Runtime error when using ExponentialMovingAverage with MirroredStrategy (TF 1.13.1)

preconditions.description: TensorFlow 1.x graph execution via tf.estimator.Estimator training (not TF2 eager-first).
Use tf.contrib.distribute.MirroredStrategy with num_gpus >= 2 (can be reproduced on CPU by specifying >=2).

trigger_features.description: Apply tf.train.ExponentialMovingAverage to tf.trainable_variables() inside the training step while training under MirroredStrategy.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Within TRAIN mode, create a tf.train.ExponentialMovingAverage and execute ema.apply(tf.trainable_variables()) (or equivalent) as part of the train_op under tf.contrib.distribute.MirroredStrategy(num_gpus>=2).
trigger_features.evidence: Issue body: "I'm trying to use ExponentialMovingAverage with MirroredStrategy ... getting an error" and shows `ema = tf.train.ExponentialMovingAverage(0.999)` then `ema_update_op = ema.apply(tf.trainable_variables())` with `distribution = tf.contrib.distribute.MirroredStrategy(num_gpus=2)`.

trigger_features.description: Instantiate the ExponentialMovingAverage object inside model_fn (or otherwise inside the per-replica graph-building context), which can cause per-replica average-variable creation with replica name segments.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Define `ema = tf.train.ExponentialMovingAverage(decay=...)` inside the estimator model_fn used with MirroredStrategy (not a global/shared instance).
trigger_features.evidence: Issue body code: `def model_fn(...): ... ema = tf.train.ExponentialMovingAverage(0.999)` and comment: "Just define your ExponentialMovingAverage outside of the training function ... Creating a global ExponentialMovingAverage instance will overcome this problem".

trigger_features.description: Have at least one trainable weight variable produced by tf.layers.dense so EMA tries to create the corresponding moving-average variable.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Include a layer that creates trainable variables (e.g., tf.layers.dense / tf.compat.v1.layers.Dense) and ensure tf.trainable_variables() is non-empty when ema.apply() runs.
trigger_features.evidence: Issue body code: `logits = tf.layers.dense(features, 1, activation=tf.nn.relu)` and the thrown variable path includes `dense/kernel/.../ExponentialMovingAverage/`.

trigger_features.description: Call ema.apply under a variable scope with reuse=tf.AUTO_REUSE, which participates in the variable creation/reuse logic during mirrored variable creation.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Wrap ema.apply(...) in `with tf.variable_scope(tf.get_variable_scope(), reuse=tf.AUTO_REUSE):` (or an equivalent variable-scope reuse pattern).
trigger_features.evidence: Issue body code: `with tf.variable_scope(tf.get_variable_scope(), reuse=tf.AUTO_REUSE): ema_update_op = ema.apply(tf.trainable_variables())`.

oracle.check: Run an estimator.train() step under MirroredStrategy(num_gpus>=2) where train_op includes ema.apply(tf.trainable_variables()).
oracle.pass_condition: Training step(s) execute without raising a RuntimeError related to variable creation/name mismatch across replicas/devices.
oracle.fail_condition: Raises `RuntimeError: Tried to create variable .../replica_1/ExponentialMovingAverage/ with mismatching name on device 1` (or equivalent message indicating mismatching variable name on device 1).
oracle.notes: Primary failure is a deterministic runtime exception during variable creation/reuse across mirrored replicas.

fix_evidence.notes: Maintainer confirms: "This was fixed in https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/commit/3a22ef3c8a466123d60c1a5d10d62e4d2d0f92d2...". Workarounds were discussed (global EMA instance; deprecated replicate_model_fn/TowerOptimizer), but an upstream fix exists.

exclusions_not_features: Dataset repeat/batch specifics (repeat(10), batch(1)) as they are not implied necessary for the variable-name mismatch.
Exact optimizer hyperparameters (learning_rate values) and choice of GradientDescentOptimizer beyond needing a train_op.
Logging verbosity and tf.logging.set_verbosity / log_step_count_steps settings.
Model directory path and file paths (e.g., 'training/test1').
User-provided hack modifying shared_variable_creator (test-harness/internal workaround code) since it is not a reusable trigger feature for generation.

bug_meta.title: [TF==2.0.0-alpha0] Memory leak with tf.keras.models.load_model

preconditions.description: TensorFlow 2.0.0 alpha / early TF2 where tf.keras manages its own graph; issue observed specifically on TF 2.0.0a0 (docker image tensorflow/tensorflow:2.0.0a0-py3-jupyter).
A Keras model saved via model.save(...) to an HDF5 .h5 file, later loaded via tf.keras.models.load_model(path).
Multiple sequential calls to load_model in the same Python process (looped loads).

trigger_features.description: Call tf.keras.backend.clear_session() immediately before each tf.keras.models.load_model(...).
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: In a loop (>=20 iterations), execute K.clear_session() right before each load_model(model_path).
trigger_features.evidence: Code to reproduce: "def load_model_keras(model_dir):\n    K.clear_session()\n    model = load_model(model_dir)" and looped loads: "for i in range(100): ... load_model_keras(model_dir)"

trigger_features.description: Repeatedly load the same .h5 model file many times without restarting the process.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Use a single .h5 path and call load_model(path) repeatedly (>=20 times).
trigger_features.evidence: Issue body: "I load 20 times a model (the same model for the example)." Comment reproduction: saves once then loads in a loop: "model.save(model_dir)" then "for i in range(20): ... load_model_keras(model_dir)"

trigger_features.description: Use a non-trivial Keras model (e.g., tf.keras.applications.ResNet50 with imagenet weights) to amplify the leak signal.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Create a model with a sizable graph/weights (e.g., ResNet50(weights='imagenet')), save to .h5, then apply the repeated load loop.
trigger_features.evidence: Comment provides example: "model = ResNet50(weights='imagenet') ... model.save(model_dir)" then repeated loading.

trigger_features.description: Memory usage increases substantially across iterations rather than stabilizing after a few loads.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Measure process memory (RSS) after each load; require monotonic or strongly increasing trend over >=20 iterations (e.g., >2x growth from baseline).
trigger_features.evidence: Issue body shows growth: first iteration ~252.9 MiB then after 20 iterations ~566.4 MiB; comment shows much larger TF2 alpha growth: first ~684.0 MiB then after 20 iterations ~3502.3 MiB.

oracle.check: Track process RSS (or equivalent) before the loop and after each load; evaluate growth across N loads (recommend N>=20).
oracle.pass_condition: Memory stabilizes after initial warmup: incremental RSS growth after iteration 5 remains small (e.g., <= 5 MiB per 10 loads) and total growth from iteration 1 to N is bounded.
oracle.fail_condition: RSS increases persistently across iterations (e.g., large positive delta per load and large total growth from iteration 1 to N, such as hundreds of MiB or more).
oracle.notes: The report used memory_profiler line-by-line increments; for discovery, any reliable RSS sampler (psutil) is acceptable. This is a memory-growth oracle, not a functional output oracle.

fix_evidence.notes: Maintainer indicates the issue is with K.clear_session not clearing the right graph in TF2 and points to a commit that "should fix the issue"; they tested on tf-nightly-2.0-preview and observed memory no longer increasing.

exclusions_not_features: Exact OS (macOS Mojave 10.14.3) and python minor version (3.5) because the trigger is described as TF2/Keras graph/session behavior rather than OS-specific.
Docker image name and Jupyter context as harness/environment packaging details (kept only the TF2 alpha constraint).
Use of memory_profiler decorator and its line-by-line table formatting; replaced by generic RSS tracking as the enforceable oracle.
Attempts like model=None, del model, gc.collect() since they were reported to have no effect and are not required to trigger the leak.
Print statements and loop counters (unittest/logging noise).

bug_meta.title: [TF 2.0] constant folding failed: invalid argument: unsupported type: 21

preconditions.description: Issue reported on TF 2.0 preview/nightly/beta builds (and also mentioned on TF 1.14 with Eager enabled).
Execution must involve graph tracing/optimization via tf.function (Grappler meta_optimizer runs).
Reports repeatedly mention the behavior under Eager execution (TF2 default; also TF1.14 when Eager is enabled).

trigger_features.description: Invoke a tf.function-wrapped training step that accepts another Python callable as an argument, where that callable is NOT itself wrapped by tf.function.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Define train(x, forward_func) and call tf.function(train)(x, forward) where forward is a plain Python function (not tf.function).
trigger_features.evidence: codes_buggy = ["tf.function(train)(x, forward)", ...] and the log shows the warning printed for that case, while "tf.function(train)(x, tf.function(forward))" is listed under codes_normal with no warning.

trigger_features.description: Use TensorFlow control flow (tf.range loop) inside the traced function (train or big_train), which lowers to tf.while_loop in graph mode.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Inside the traced function, iterate `for i in tf.range(batch_size): ...` where batch_size depends on input shape.
trigger_features.evidence: for i in tf.range(batch_size): y = model(x[i][tf.newaxis, :]) ... (appears in forward and big_train). Another commenter: "everything runs without a hitch if the for loop (tf.while_loop behind the scenes) is removed".

trigger_features.description: Accumulate per-iteration outputs using tf.TensorArray.write and then stack, inside a tf.function-traced region (either directly or via a passed callable).
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Create `ys = tf.TensorArray(tf.float32, size=batch_size)`; in loop do `ys = ys.write(i, y)`; return `ys.stack()` (or do this inside a function called from the traced function).
trigger_features.evidence: ys = tf.TensorArray(tf.float32, size=batch_size) ... ys = ys.write(i, y) ... return ys.stack() and the warning appears for tf.function(train)(x, forward) and tf.function(big_train)(x).

trigger_features.description: Compute gradients with tf.GradientTape where the forward path includes control-flow + TensorArray patterns under tf.function tracing.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Wrap a function containing `with tf.GradientTape() as tape: ys = forward_func(x); loss = tf.reduce_mean(ys)` and compute `tape.gradient(loss, model.trainable_weights)`; trace the outer function with tf.function.
trigger_features.evidence: def train(x, forward_func): with tf.GradientTape() as tape: ys = forward_func(x) ... grads = tape.gradient(loss, model.trainable_weights). Buggy call shown: tf.function(train)(x, forward).

trigger_features.description: Train a Keras model containing GRU/LSTM with masking over variable-length sequences; reported to correlate with the warning and (in some reports) severe memory blow-up/crash during fit.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Build a model with tf.keras.layers.LSTM or GRU and pass a boolean mask (e.g., mask input or tf.sequence_mask) for variable-length padded sequences; call model.fit.
trigger_features.evidence: User report: "run into this issue when using masking on a GRU/LSTM layer ... memory ... crashing ... Removing the masking allows training ... though the 'constant folding failed ... Unsupported type: 21' message still occurs." Another reproduction shows mask inputs to BiLSTM and failure during model.fit with GPU OOM + Killed.

oracle.check: Detect presence of Grappler meta_optimizer warning/error text indicating constant folding failure for unsupported type 21 during tracing/first execution.
oracle.pass_condition: No log line containing "constant folding failed: Invalid argument: Unsupported type: 21" during execution of the test case.
oracle.fail_condition: Log contains "constant folding failed: Invalid argument: Unsupported type: 21" (often printed twice) during tf.function execution / first model.fit call.
oracle.notes: This is a warning/optimizer error, not necessarily a functional correctness failure. It can still be used as a discovery oracle because it indicates an optimizer failure mode and was linked to severe slowdowns and, in some reports, memory blow-up.
oracle.evidence: 2019-06-07 ... E tensorflow/core/grappler/optimizers/meta_optimizer.cc:502] constant folding failed: Invalid argument: Unsupported type: 21 (printed for tf.function(train)(x, forward) and tf.function(big_train)(x)); later: "still shows up twice when first calling the fit method".

oracle.check: Run model.fit under GPU and/or CPU and monitor for OOM allocation failures and process termination.
oracle.pass_condition: Training completes at least one epoch/step without CUDA/host allocation OOM and without process termination.
oracle.fail_condition: OOM errors occur (e.g., CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY / could not allocate pinned host memory) and/or process gets killed during model.fit.
oracle.notes: This oracle is higher discovery value but may be hardware-dependent; keep it gated behind GPU + masking preconditions.
oracle.evidence: With GPU enabled: "failed to alloc ... CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY ... Killed" during model.fit in the BiLSTM masking example.

fix_evidence.notes: TF maintainer states the warning should go away in the next nightly and identifies the cause as Grappler constant folding failing due to DT_VARIANT handling (ZerosLike overloaded for DT_VARIANT). Fix submitted in commit 24174643a75e819b8ce01fd70d45d03616e50071.

exclusions_not_features: Exact timestamps and log prefixes (date/time, file names like meta_optimizer.cc:502) beyond the core message string
Build/install details like 'binary', 'pip', or OS distro names unless needed to enforce GPU presence
Performance numbers (seconds/batch, slowdown factors) because they are not stable oracles for automated bug discovery
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES toggling instructions (treated as diagnostic, not an indispensable trigger)
TensorBoard visualization color/device tracing discussion (diagnostic noise)
References to related issues (#28626, #30263, #29189) without additional indispensable trigger constraints
Unverified speculation about CuDNN kernel selection (not used as a trigger unless explicitly confirmed as required)

bug_meta.title: TPU has XLA compilation issue on TF 1.14

preconditions.description: TensorFlow v1 graph/session workflow using tf.contrib.compiler.xla.compile (TF 1.13.x–1.14.0 reported; TF 2.0.0a0 cannot run due to missing tensorflow.contrib).
Reproduced on Cloud TPU and also in Colab TPU (report + maintainer reproduction).
Graph includes an optimizer minimize() path (GradientDescentOptimizer.minimize(loss)) so gradients and aggregation are built.

trigger_features.description: XLA encapsulates a subgraph into a function and Grappler optimizes the function library; the memory optimizer injects a tmp_var node that becomes a TemporaryVariable in the XLA-compiled cluster.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Compile a training step with tf.contrib.compiler.xla.compile (or XLA JIT scope) such that the compiled region is encapsulated into a function and then passed through Grappler function-library optimization (default settings).
trigger_features.evidence: ezhulenev: "XLA encapsulates subgraph into a function" and "Grappler optimizes function library, and memory optimizer adds \"tmp_var\" node".

trigger_features.description: The compiled XLA cluster contains a TemporaryVariable op, which is unsupported for XLA JIT devices, causing compilation failure.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Ensure the compiled region includes an op path that results in a TemporaryVariable node inside the XLA cluster (e.g., tmp_var created under gradients/AddN... during training graph construction).
trigger_features.evidence: Error: "Detected unsupported operations ... on XLA_CPU_JIT: TemporaryVariable (No registered 'TemporaryVariable' OpKernel for XLA_CPU_JIT devices compatible with node {{node gradients/AddN_13/tmp_var}})".

trigger_features.description: Using large Transformer-like dimensions triggers the failing graph shape/structure; reducing HIDDEN_SIZE/FILTER_SIZE/NUM_HEADS by 4 avoids the issue.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Use large dimensions comparable to HIDDEN_SIZE=2048, FILTER_SIZE=8196, NUM_HEADS=32 and WORD_LEN=512 (or similarly large) so the same model structure triggers the TemporaryVariable insertion; verify that scaling these down (e.g., /4) removes the failure.
trigger_features.evidence: Reporter: "The issue can actually be avoided ... change HIDDEN_SIZE=2048, FILTER_SIZE=8196, NUM_HEADS=32 ... to ... //4 ... The fix above where I divide the numbers by 4 also fixes the issue."

trigger_features.description: Inputs are provided via a tf.data iterator get_next() fed directly into xla.compile for a train-mode EstimatorSpec loss/train_op function.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Build a tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices over tensors shaped like [1, WORD_LEN, HIDDEN_SIZE] (features) and [1,1,1,WORD_LEN] (labels/bias), create an Iterator.from_structure, and pass iterator.get_next() as inputs to tf.contrib.compiler.xla.compile wrapping a model_fn that returns loss under control_dependencies([train_op]).
trigger_features.evidence: issue.py: "iterator = tf.data.Iterator.from_structure(...); loss, = compile(xla_model_fn, inputs=iterator.get_next()); ... with tf.control_dependencies([spec.train_op]): return tf.identity(spec.loss)"

trigger_features.description: Switching to resource variables (tf.enable_resource_variables + use_resource=True) does not prevent the TemporaryVariable failure in this report.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Even if enabling resource variables globally and using use_resource=True for tf.get_variable, keep the rest of the graph the same; do not assume this change removes TemporaryVariable insertion.
trigger_features.evidence: Reporter: "I enabled resource variables ... I still get the same issue."

oracle.check: Run a Session on the compiled loss op (sess.run(loss)) after initializing variables and iterator; capture exceptions from XLA compilation/execution.
oracle.pass_condition: No exception raised during compilation/execution of the compiled loss op.
oracle.fail_condition: InvalidArgumentError raised stating unsupported operations in XLA cluster due to TemporaryVariable / missing OpKernel for XLA_* device (often referencing gradients/.../tmp_var).

fix_evidence.patch_snippet:
Replace TensorArray-based storage with Tensor/Variable buffers and use scatter/gather ops:

- `tf.gather(self.obs_buf, idxs)`

bug_meta.title: Keras model saving erroring: TypeError: get_config() missing 1 required positional argument: 'self'

trigger_features.description: Provide a Keras layer initializer as a callable/class reference (no parentheses) instead of an instantiated initializer object, so serialization later tries to call get_config on a non-instance.

trigger_features.description: Trigger occurs specifically during model.save when Keras serializes layer configs (including initializers) and attempts to call get_config.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Call model.save(export_dir) on a built tf.keras.Model (SavedModel export), after at least one forward pass/build (e.g., model.predict on dummy input) to ensure weights exist.

trigger_features.description: Using a class-reference initializer does not necessarily error during model build/predict/train, but fails later when saving.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Run a forward pass (predict) or minimal compile/train step successfully with the class-reference initializer, then attempt model.save and observe failure.

oracle.fail_condition: model.save raises TypeError containing "get_config() missing 1 required positional argument: 'self'".

bug_meta.title: [TFLite] Segmentation fault on inference due to int overflow in im2col

preconditions.description: Run inference using the TensorFlow Lite Interpreter on a converted TFLite model.
Model execution must use the optimized Conv kernel path that performs im2col (not the reference kernels).
Conversion applies TFLite default optimization (quantization/hybrid path may be selected).
Inference is executed on CPU (TFLite optimized ops / CpuBackendContext shown in stack trace).

trigger_features.description: Construct a Conv2D in the executed graph such that the im2col temporary buffer element count overflows 32-bit int indexing (or is otherwise large enough to cause negative/invalid int indices during im2col).
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Ensure at least one executed Conv2D has output_height*output_width*input_depth*filter_height*filter_width*batches > 2_147_483_647 (INT32_MAX).
trigger_features.evidence: “The last convolution needs an im2col buffer of size `1*2800*2800*(32*3*3) = 2 257 920 000` which is larger than the 32-bit `int` used for indexing in `Im2col` and result in a `Segmentation fault` … due to some of the indexes going negative”

trigger_features.description: Use a super-resolution-style model (or any model) that expands spatial resolution significantly so the last convolution operates on very large output height/width.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Use an input tensor with large spatial dims and a model that scales output spatial dims by ~4x (e.g., 700x700 -> 2800x2800) so that the final Conv2D runs at the large resolution.
trigger_features.evidence: “Such large buffers can quickly happen in super resolution models with large output resolution… It uses a larger 700x700 input image to generate a 2800x2800 output image.”

trigger_features.description: Convert a SavedModel concrete function (e.g., TF Hub ESRGAN) to TFLite and invoke it without feeding inputs (still executes the graph / alloc + invoke).
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Load a TF Hub model, take DEFAULT_SERVING_SIGNATURE_DEF_KEY concrete function, set input shape to (1, 700, 700, 3) (or other size meeting overflow), convert via TFLiteConverter.from_concrete_functions, then Interpreter.allocate_tensors() and Interpreter.invoke().
trigger_features.evidence: Code snippet in issue: `model = hub.load("https://tfhub.dev/captain-pool/esrgan-tf2/1") ... converter = tf.lite.TFLiteConverter.from_concrete_functions([concrete_func]) ... interpreter.allocate_tensors(); interpreter.invoke()`

trigger_features.description: Execution goes through the hybrid per-channel convolution implementation that calls optimized im2col.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Enable a conversion/config where Conv executes as hybrid per-channel (typical with Optimize.DEFAULT) so stack includes HybridConvPerChannel and Im2col on int8 (`signed char`) buffers.
trigger_features.evidence: Stack trace shows: `tflite::optimized_ops::Im2col<signed char>` and `tflite::optimized_ops::HybridConvPerChannel(...)`

trigger_features.description: Forcing reference kernels (disabling optimized im2col path) avoids the crash; this is a negative-control constraint to validate the trigger is tied to optimized im2col.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Run the same TFLite model with a configuration that forces reference kernels; expect no crash (used to confirm the bug is specific to optimized im2col path).
trigger_features.evidence: “Forcing the usage of the reference kernels which don't use the im2col optimization circumvent the problem.”

oracle.check: Execute `interpreter.allocate_tensors()` then `interpreter.invoke()` on the produced TFLite model and detect process crash (SIGSEGV) or abnormal termination; optionally match crash location in optimized im2col.
oracle.pass_condition: Process completes invocation without crashing.
oracle.fail_condition: Segmentation fault / SIGSEGV occurs during or inside `interpreter.invoke()` (often within `tflite::optimized_ops::Im2col<signed char>`).
oracle.notes: This is a strong discovery oracle because it is a hard crash. Matching stack frames is optional; crash alone is sufficient.

fix_evidence.notes: Maintainer states a fix to “skip such im2col operation but fallbacks to a not-well-optimized CONV implementation when this tensor is over 1GB.” Reporter confirms the fix resolves the issue on the provided repro and another affected model.

exclusions_not_features: Exact build/OS details implied by stack trace (x86_64 memmove assembly frame) since architecture-specific frame is not required to trigger the overflow condition.
Exact number of threads (`num_threads=os.cpu_count()`) because threading is not presented as necessary for reproduction.
Full stack trace lines and memory addresses (kept only as minimal evidence for im2col/hybrid path).
Blog tutorial link and general discussion about super-resolution (kept only the enforceable scale-up constraint).
Speculative root-cause beyond what the issue and maintainer explicitly state (e.g., internal indexing implementation details not quoted).

bug_meta.title: model.fit with dataset generator results in deadlock/hang

preconditions.description: TensorFlow 2.5.0 (reported reproducible/hangs).

bug_meta.title: tf.keras.layers.MaxPooling3D crashes

preconditions.description: TensorFlow 2.6.0 and earlier are affected; behavior is reported fixed starting in 2.6.1+.
On CPU in TF 2.6.0 and earlier, invalid pool_size can abort the process with a floating point exception.
Bug manifests via Keras 3D pooling layers and also when the underlying TF op max_pool3d is invoked through layer call.

trigger_features.description: Provide a 3D pooling pool_size with at least one dimension equal to 0 (e.g., [2,2,0]) when calling 3D pooling.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Construct MaxPooling3D (or AveragePooling3D) with pool_size where any element == 0; call layer on a valid 5D input tensor (N,D,H,W,C).
trigger_features.evidence: `tf.keras.layers.MaxPooling3D` crashes when `pool_size` contains `0` ... pool_size = [2, 2, 0] ... res = layer(input_tensor) # crash ... Output: Floating point exception (core dumped)

trigger_features.description: Provide a 3D pooling pool_size with a negative dimension (e.g., [2,2,-2]) causing non-finite outputs (all inf) instead of rejecting invalid configuration.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Construct MaxPooling3D with pool_size where any element < 0; call layer on a valid 5D float input; check output for non-finite values (inf).
trigger_features.evidence: `tf.keras.layers.MaxPooling3D` ... outputs a all-inf tensor when `pool_size` contains negative values. ... pool_size = [2, 2, -2] ... The output is a tensor ... and all `inf` values.

trigger_features.description: AveragePooling3D also crashes when pool_size contains 0 (same invalid input validation gap).
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Construct AveragePooling3D with pool_size where any element == 0; call on a valid 5D input tensor; observe crash/abort in affected versions on CPU.
trigger_features.evidence: Comment: `tf.keras.layers.AveragePooling3D` also crashes when `pool_size` contains `0`.

trigger_features.description: Multiple API aliases hit the same invalid pool_size=0 crash on older TF versions (tf.keras.* and tf.compat.v1.keras.* aliases).
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Use any of: tf.keras.layers.MaxPool3D / MaxPooling3D / tf.compat.v1.keras.layers.MaxPool3D / MaxPooling3D (and similarly AvgPool3D/AveragePooling3D) with pool_size containing 0; call on valid 5D input.
trigger_features.evidence: Comment lists aliases causing same issue: `tf.keras.layers.MaxPooling3D`, `tf.keras.layers.MaxPool3D`, `tf.compat.v1.keras.layers.MaxPooling3D`, `tf.compat.v1.keras.layers.MaxPool3D` and similarly for AveragePooling3D/AvgPool3D; and shows pool_size=[2,2,0] reproducer ending with `Floating point exception(core dumped)` on CPU.

trigger_features.description: With invalid pool_size=0 in older versions, CPU can hard-abort while GPU throws a catchable InternalError (dnn PoolForward launch failed).
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Run same pool_size=[2,2,0] pooling3D call on CPU-only vs GPU-enabled runtime; compare failure types (process abort vs thrown exception).
trigger_features.evidence: Comment: On CPU it aborts with `Floating point exception(core dumped)`; on GPU it throws `tensorflow.python.framework.errors_impl.InternalError: dnn PoolForward launch failed [Op:MaxPool3D]`.

oracle.check: Execute the pooling call in a subprocess (or equivalent isolation) and detect abnormal termination (non-zero exit) with a message indicating floating point exception/core dump.
oracle.pass_condition: Process remains alive and raises a Python-level validation error for invalid pool_size (ValueError/InvalidArgumentError).
oracle.fail_condition: Process aborts/terminates (e.g., 'Floating point exception (core dumped)').
oracle.notes: Use isolation because this is a hard crash on CPU in affected versions; do not rely on unittest harness output.

oracle.check: After calling MaxPooling3D with negative pool_size, test that output tensor contains any non-finite values (is_inf / is_finite).
oracle.pass_condition: Invalid pool_size is rejected via ValueError/InvalidArgumentError before producing output.
oracle.fail_condition: Call returns a tensor with all or some entries == inf (non-finite).
oracle.notes: Prefer a non-finite check over exact shape/value checks; shape in the report is incidental.

oracle.check: Construct pooling layer with pool_size containing 0 or negative and call it; assert a validation exception is raised.
oracle.pass_condition: Raises ValueError (or InvalidArgumentError in TF 2.6.1 per report) for invalid pool_size.
oracle.fail_condition: No exception raised, or crash/abort, or non-finite output produced.

fix_evidence.notes: A Keras PR is referenced: keras-team/keras#15356. A TF maintainer notes a TF-side fix PR (#51975) was created to fix inside TensorFlow. A later comment reports the behavior is fixed in TF 2.6.1+ with InvalidArgumentError/ValueError instead of CPU abort or inf outputs.

bug_meta.title: Using `+` in custom residual Keras `Layer` does not create correct model graph

preconditions.description: Observed on TensorFlow v2.8.0-rc1 (2.8.0); reporter also notes reproducibility on hosted notebooks (Kaggle/Colab) with and without GPU.
Custom residual block implemented as a Keras Layer with a Python loop over sub-blocks inside call(), updating x each iteration.
Bug manifests during training/backpropagation (gradients), not in forward-only execution.

trigger_features.description: Use the Python `+` operator to add two tensors inside a Keras Layer.call() to form a residual/skip connection (x = x + h) within a loop.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Define a tf.keras.layers.Layer subclass whose call() computes h from x and then sets x = x + h at least once (preferably multiple times in a loop).
trigger_features.evidence:
In custom residual block implementation with keras APIs, `+` yields broken graph.

```python
x = x + h
```

trigger_features.description: Apply the residual add multiple times in a loop (stacked residual blocks), increasing the chance the malformed graph breaks skip connectivity during training.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Within call(), iterate over >=2 residual sub-blocks and perform x = x + h each iteration (e.g., blocks=2).
trigger_features.evidence:
Standalone repro uses `ResBlock(2, True)` and inside call():
```python
for block in self.blocks:
    ...
    x = x + h if self.shortcut else h
```

trigger_features.description: Forward pass outputs match between the `+` implementation and an explicit Add-layer implementation under deterministic ops, but training gradients differ enough to prevent convergence.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Run two models: (A) residual via `+`, (B) residual via dedicated tf.keras.layers.Add instances; verify forward outputs match (within 0 tolerance for deterministic settings) but training/gradients diverge (e.g., gradient tensors differ or loss fails to decrease for (A) while (B) learns).
trigger_features.evidence: “Both versions of the code work during the forward pass. When setting random seeds and `TF_DETERMINISTIC_OPS=1`, **the outputs of each version are identical**. Problems only appear during training because the gradients are not computed correctly for the `+`-version due to the malformed computation graph...”

trigger_features.description: Even if the internal ops are pure TensorFlow (e.g., tf.nn.conv2d) rather than Keras layers, the issue persists when the residual logic lives inside a Keras Layer subclass; a fully non-Keras (plain Python object) version does not show the same trace issue.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Implement residual block as tf.keras.layers.Layer but compute h using pure tf ops (e.g., tf.nn.conv2d with a constant kernel) and still use x = x + h; optionally compare to a plain Python object implementing __call__ with the same logic.
trigger_features.evidence: “The Keras version is still broken on tensorboard, but the pure version with no Keras APIs appears to work fine.”

oracle.check: Build two equivalent networks: one using `x = x + h` in a Keras Layer, the other using explicit `tf.keras.layers.Add` instances (`add([x,h])`). Run a single training step on identical inputs/targets with the same initialization and deterministic settings; compare gradients (e.g., max_abs_diff over each variable's gradient) or compare parameter updates.
oracle.pass_condition: Gradients (or parameter updates) are equivalent within a tight tolerance between the `+` model and the Add-layer baseline.
oracle.fail_condition: At least one trainable variable has gradient mismatch beyond tolerance between the `+` model and the Add-layer baseline, or the `+` model fails to reduce loss across steps while the baseline does.
oracle.notes: Reporter states forward outputs are identical under `TF_DETERMINISTIC_OPS=1` but gradients are not computed correctly for the `+` version, causing failure to converge.

oracle.check: Train the `+` residual model and the Add-layer residual model for N steps on a simple supervised task; track loss curve.
oracle.pass_condition: Both variants show comparable loss reduction.
oracle.fail_condition: Add-layer variant learns (loss decreases) but the `+` variant fails to learn (loss stagnates) under otherwise identical setup.
oracle.notes: This oracle is weaker than direct gradient comparison, but aligns with the issue report: “My model would not train… serious issues with my gradients… model could not learn.”

fix_evidence.patch_snippet:
Replace `x = x + h` with a dedicated Add layer per residual step, e.g.:
```python
for block, add in zip(self.blocks, self.adds):
    ...
    x = add([x, h])
```
fix_evidence.notes: The TensorFlow issue was closed after redirecting to the Keras repo; within this report, the only confirmed remediation is using explicit `keras.layers.Add` instances instead of `+`.

exclusions_not_features: Model plot/visualization details (plot_model wrapper, expand_nested/show_shapes)
OS details (MacOS 10.15.6) and Python version (3.7.12) unless needed
Build/installation method (binary install)
Hosted environment names (Kaggle/Colab) and presence/absence of GPU (not required to trigger)
TensorBoard tracing mechanics (used as evidence/inspection, not required to reproduce the gradient issue)
Exact convolution configuration in ConvBnAct (kernel sizes/BN/activation) beyond 'compute h from x'

bug_meta.title: gradient tape with rank 0 tensors causes integer division or modulo by zero

preconditions.description: Reported on TensorFlow 2.3.1 (binary install), Python 3.8.x, Ubuntu 20.04; repro uses eager execution with tf.GradientTape.

trigger_features.description: Index a tensor all the way down to a scalar (rank-0) inside GradientTape (e.g., model(x)[0,0]) and then use that scalar in downstream ops used by the loss.

trigger_features.description: Compute trigonometric ops on the scalar theta (cos/sin) inside the tape, feeding their results into the loss construction.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Compute a = tf.math.cos(theta) and b = tf.math.sin(theta) where theta is rank-0, and use [a, b] as the immediate inputs to loss aggregation.
trigger_features.evidence: Repro code: `theta = model(x)[0,0]` then `loss = tf.concat([tf.math.cos(theta), tf.math.sin(theta)], axis=0)`.

trigger_features.description: Construct the loss by concatenating scalar tensors (rank-0) with tf.concat along axis 0, yielding an error during backprop.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Use `loss = tf.concat([scalar1, scalar2], axis=0)` where scalar1 and scalar2 are rank-0 (produced from ops on a rank-0 theta).
trigger_features.evidence: Issue body repro uses `loss = tf.concat([tf.math.cos(theta), tf.math.sin(theta)], axis=0)` and the traceback ends with `ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero` from `_ConcatGradHelper`.

oracle.pass_condition: No exception is raised by tape.gradient; gradients are returned (or a meaningful TensorFlow error, not a Python ZeroDivisionError).
oracle.fail_condition: A Python `ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero` is raised during gradient computation (notably from concat gradient path).
oracle.notes: Traceback in report shows ZeroDivisionError arising in `tensorflow/python/ops/array_grad.py` within concat gradient helper.

Since `tf.concat()` doesn’t have keepdims argument, replace it with `tf.math.reduce_mean()`...

bug_meta.title: tensorflow_model_optimization,quantization.keras.quantize_model raises exception on its documentation example

preconditions.description: tensorflow_model_optimization is installed and tfmot.quantization.keras.quantize_model is used.
Environment has both `keras` (standalone Keras 3-style package) and `tf_keras` available, making it possible to pass a model object from one distribution into APIs expecting the other.
Reported on TensorFlow 2.16.1 and also reproduced on TF nightly according to the issue template.

trigger_features.description: Call tfmot.quantization.keras.quantize_model with a model created via `keras.Sequential` (standalone keras), not `tf_keras.Sequential`.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Construct model using `import keras` and `keras.Sequential([...])`, then call `tfmot.quantization.keras.quantize_model(model)`.
trigger_features.evidence: Traceback shows ValueError when called with `keras.Sequential([...])`: `ValueError: `to_quantize` can only either be a keras Sequential or Functional model.`

trigger_features.description: Import `keras` and `layers` from `keras` rather than from `tf_keras` (or tf.keras), then build the Sequential model.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Use `import keras` and `from keras import layers` before building the model passed to tfmot.
trigger_features.evidence: Failing repro uses: `import keras` / `from keras import layers` and then passes `keras.Sequential([...])` into `tfmot.quantization.keras.quantize_model(...)`.

trigger_features.description: Model is a simple Sequential stack of Dense layers with `input_shape=(100,)` specified on the first Dense layer (as in the documentation example).
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Build `Sequential([Dense(10, activation='relu', input_shape=(100,)), Dense(2, activation='sigmoid')])` and pass into tfmot quantize_model.
trigger_features.evidence: Repro code includes: `layers.Dense(10, activation='relu', input_shape=(100,)), layers.Dense(2, activation='sigmoid')`.

oracle.check: Execute the quantize_model call and catch exceptions.
oracle.pass_condition: No exception is raised and a quantized model object is returned.
oracle.fail_condition: Raises ValueError with message indicating the input can only be a keras Sequential or Functional model.
oracle.notes: This is a robust oracle because it is an immediate API-level failure signal (exception).

oracle.check: Run the same quantize_model call twice: once using `keras.Sequential` and once using `tf_keras.Sequential` with identical layers.
oracle.pass_condition: Both succeed (or both fail) consistently for the same model structure.
oracle.fail_condition: `keras.Sequential` path fails with ValueError while `tf_keras.Sequential` path succeeds.
oracle.notes: Use this as a stronger discovery oracle for future regressions: differential behavior across Keras distributions indicates a compatibility boundary.

fix_evidence.notes: Reporter states the workaround: use `tf_keras.Sequential` (and `from tf_keras import layers`) instead of `keras.Sequential`, because the classes are different. No official patch/commit is provided in the issue content.

exclusions_not_features: GPU model, CUDA/cuDNN versions, and device initialization logs (not needed to trigger the exception).
UserWarning about passing input_shape to Dense (warning noise; not required to trigger the ValueError).
Python REPL transcript formatting, timestamps, and filesystem paths in stacktrace.

bug_meta.title: losses return None if dictionary is used in pipeline and model

preconditions.description: TensorFlow >= 2.16.2 (reported failing on 2.16.2 and 2.17.0); reportedly worked on 2.14.1.
Keras Model compiled with a standard loss (e.g., SparseCategoricalCrossentropy) and trained via model.fit on a tf.data.Dataset.
tf.data pipeline returns (x, y) where y is a dict with a single key.
Keras model outputs are provided as a dict (single-output wrapped in dict).

trigger_features.description: Training fails when the dict key used for y_true in the dataset does not match the model's output naming used by compile/loss mapping (dict key / output name).
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Create a tf.data.Dataset where map_fn returns y as {'K1': y}, but build a Keras model whose output mapping resolves to a different name/key (e.g., outputs={'K2': tensor} and/or last layer name != K1). Keep loss as a single loss object (not dict). Call model.fit; expect failure.
trigger_features.evidence: Issue body: "If you run this code with tf>=2.16.2, it will fail with \"no loss function\" error (see the map_fct output returns \"custom_out\") as well as the model definition uses \"custom_out\". If you change the map_fct and the model definition to remove the dictionary, it is working." + Log: "ValueError: No loss to compute. Provide a `loss` argument in `compile()`."

trigger_features.description: To make dict-based dataset labels and dict-based model outputs work, the dataset y_true key, the model output dict key, and (at least) the final layer name must be consistent; otherwise the trainer cannot flatten/map y and y_pred for loss computation.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Run two variants: (A) mismatch names across dataset key/model output key/last layer name -> expect failure; (B) set all three to the same string -> expect training to proceed and produce finite loss/metrics.
trigger_features.evidence: Comment (just-sabyr): "It looks like all of the three output names (outputs Dense(10) layer, dataset y_true label name, model_outputs name) have to be called by the same name." and provides working code where map_fct returns {'y_true': y}, last Dense is named 'y_true', and model outputs={'y_true': outputs}.

trigger_features.description: When using a single (non-dict) loss in compile(), dict-structured y/y_pred with non-matching keys can lead to the trainer concluding there is 'No loss to compute'.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Compile with loss=SparseCategoricalCrossentropy() (single object) while feeding dict labels and dict outputs with mismatched keys; call model.fit; assert the specific ValueError is raised.
trigger_features.evidence: Log: "ValueError: No loss to compute. Provide a `loss` argument in `compile()`." with compile() already specifying a loss; comment (just-sabyr): "However there should be a proper error handling to warn users about non-matching dict keys."

oracle.check: Execute model.fit(train_dataset, validation_data=val_dataset) after compile(loss=SparseCategoricalCrossentropy()) with dict y_true and dict outputs using mismatched names/keys.
oracle.pass_condition: Training starts and returns a History object with a numeric loss value for the first batch/epoch.
oracle.fail_condition: Raises ValueError indicating no loss can be computed (despite loss being provided).
oracle.notes: Robust discovery oracle: the exception message suggests the trainer failed to map dict outputs/labels to the configured loss.

fix_evidence.notes: No upstream patch is shown in the thread; the provided resolution is a naming workaround: align dataset dict key, model output dict key, and final layer name.

exclusions_not_features: oneDNN, cuFFT/cuDNN/cuBLAS registration warnings and TF-TRT warning
GPU model/memory details and CUDA availability
Rocky Linux / exact file paths in traceback
AUTOTUNE, num_parallel_calls, and batching/drop_remainder specifics (not indicated as indispensable to trigger)
MNIST dataset choice and exact network architecture depth (Dense layers are just a minimal reproducer)
pip install lines from comment (environment setup noise)

bug_meta.title: Failing to convert MobileNetV3Large to TFLite w/ Integer q

preconditions.description: Use Keras MobileNetV3Large with ImageNet weights, include_top=True, input_shape=(224,224,3), and run inference on a float32 NHWC tensor shaped (1,224,224,3).
Convert the model to TFLite using TFLiteConverter with optimizations=[tf.lite.Optimize.DEFAULT] (post-training quantization path).
Converter target_spec.supported_ops includes both TFLITE_BUILTINS and SELECT_TF_OPS.
Use the SavedModel export path (model.export(saved_model_path) then TFLiteConverter.from_saved_model(saved_model_path)).

trigger_features.description: Setting converter.representative_dataset while using Optimize.DEFAULT causes a large quality regression in TFLite outputs versus the original Keras model (correlation drops substantially).
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Define converter.representative_dataset = representative_dataset where representative_dataset yields a sequence of float32 tensors of shape (1,224,224,3) and run converter.convert() with converter.optimizations=[tf.lite.Optimize.DEFAULT].
trigger_features.evidence: Comment shows regression when toggling representative dataset: "self_contained_example(add_representative_dataset=False)... Prediction correlation: 0.9775" vs "self_contained_example(add_representative_dataset=True)... Prediction correlation: 0.5212" and "the results actually get much worse!"

trigger_features.description: Representative dataset yields float32 samples clipped to [0,255] (random normal) with NHWC shape (1,224,224,3).
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: representative_dataset() yields [np.clip(np.random.normal(127.5,50,(1,224,224,3)),0,255).astype(np.float32)] for N>=50 samples.
trigger_features.evidence: User-provided fully reproducible code: "for _ in range(100): sample = np.random.normal(loc=127.5, scale=50, size=(1, 224, 224, 3)); sample = np.clip(sample, 0, 255).astype(np.float32); yield [sample]"

trigger_features.description: Running inference via tf.lite.Interpreter (which typically uses XNNPACK delegate on CPU) exposes either quality regression or runtime failure for representative-dataset converted model.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Create tf.lite.Interpreter(model_content=tflite_model), call allocate_tensors(), set input tensor, invoke(), then read output tensor; treat delegate runtime creation failure as a failure signal.
trigger_features.evidence: User reports runtime failure with representative dataset on TF 2.17: "RuntimeError: failed to create XNNPACK runtimeNode number 131 (TfLiteXNNPackDelegate) failed to prepare."

trigger_features.description: Compare original Keras model predictions vs TFLite predictions on the same input; correlation degrades sharply when representative_dataset is enabled.
trigger_features.enforceable_constraint: Compute Pearson correlation between flatten(original_pred) and flatten(tflite_pred); flag if correlation < 0.8 (or if it drops by >= 0.3 relative to no-representative baseline).
trigger_features.evidence: User provides correlation metric and values: "Prediction correlation: 0.9775" without representative dataset vs "Prediction correlation: 0.5212" with representative dataset; earlier also notes extreme failure: "Prediction correlation is -0.0192" in a reproduction.

oracle.check: Run two conversions of the same SavedModel with identical settings except converter.representative_dataset: (A) unset, (B) set. For the same input tensor, compute Pearson correlation between original Keras output and each TFLite output. Also compute delta = corr(A) - corr(B).
oracle.pass_condition: corr(B) is close to corr(A) (e.g., corr(B) >= 0.9 AND delta <= 0.1).
oracle.fail_condition: corr(B) is substantially worse than corr(A) (e.g., corr(B) < 0.8 OR delta >= 0.3).
oracle.notes: Evidence shows corr(A) ~0.9775 while corr(B) ~0.5212 under the same pipeline.

oracle.check: After converting with converter.representative_dataset set, instantiate tf.lite.Interpreter(model_content=tflite_model) and call allocate_tensors()/invoke().
oracle.pass_condition: Interpreter allocates tensors and invoke() completes without exception.
oracle.fail_condition: RuntimeError during interpreter creation or invoke, including XNNPACK delegate prepare failures.
oracle.notes: Reported error: "RuntimeError: failed to create XNNPACK runtimeNode number 131 (TfLiteXNNPackDelegate) failed to prepare."

fix_evidence.notes: No confirmed upstream patch is provided in the thread. A suggested workaround is to change the conversion approach (use Keras 3 export + from_saved_model) and/or specific TF/Keras version combinations; however, the reporter states the representative-dataset degradation persists across TF 2.10, 2.13, 2.14, and 2.16, and also reports an XNNPACK runtime failure in TF 2.17 when representative_dataset is enabled.

exclusions_not_features: OS differences (Windows 10 vs WSL) — not shown to be indispensable once the repro is in Colab/various versions.
GPU/CPU availability logs and CUDA registration warnings — unrelated to the core conversion + inference mismatch trigger.
Plotting/visualization code (matplotlib scatter/hist) — used for diagnosis, not needed to trigger or detect failure.
Size reporting and 'ignored output_format/drop_control_dependency' logs — conversion noise, not a trigger.

converter._experimental_disable_per_channel and converter.experimental_new_converter flags from the original body — later repro code/comments do not require them for the representative-dataset regression.
